questions.question: Describe the three mother graphs on [−360°; 360°] — starting behaviour, amplitude, period, and any asymptotes — and explain why tangent's period is half the others'.
questions.expected_answer: y = sin x starts at zero climbing, with amplitude 1 and period 360°, peaking at 90° and dipping to −1 at 270°. y = cos x is the same wave starting at its maximum of 1, amplitude 1, period 360°; it is sine shifted 90° to the left. y = tan x passes through zero at 0°, reaches 1 at 45°, and shoots up towards vertical asymptotes at 90° + k·180° (on this interval: −270°, −90°, 90°, 270°); it has no amplitude because each branch takes every real value, and its period is 180°. The half-period follows from the reduction formulae: sin(180° + θ) = −sinθ and cos(180° + θ) = −cosθ, so their quotient is unchanged after half a turn — tan(180° + θ) = tanθ — while sine and cosine individually need a full 360° to return to the same value.

questions.question: For y = 2 sin x + 1, determine the amplitude, middle line, range, and the positions of the maximum and minimum, and show how to run the reading backwards from a sketch with top 3 and bottom −1.
questions.expected_answer: The a = 2 doubles every height, so the amplitude is 2; the q = 1 lifts the middle line to y = 1. The wave swings from 1 − 2 = −1 up to 1 + 2 = 3, so the range is [−1; 3], with square brackets because a sine wave genuinely reaches its peak and floor. The maximum of 3 occurs where sine peaks, at x = 90° (plus multiples of 360°), and the minimum of −1 at x = 270°. Reading backwards: the middle line is the average of top and bottom, (3 + (−1))/2 = 1, so q = 1; the amplitude is half the total swing, (3 − (−1))/2 = 2, so a = 2 — recovering y = 2 sin x + 1. The common error is taking the whole swing of 4 as the amplitude instead of half.

questions.question: Sketch-plan y = 2 cos(x − 60°) on [0°; 360°]: give the four-step order, the transformed anchor points, and the y-intercept check.
questions.expected_answer: Order: shape, shift, stretch, check. Shape: the cosine skeleton — maximum, zero, minimum, zero, maximum at the quarter marks. Shift: the bracket is zero at x = 60°, so every anchor slides 60° right: maximum at 60°, descending zero at 150°, minimum at 240°, ascending zero at 330°; the next maximum at 420° falls outside the window, so the curve enters the window partway up on the left. Stretch: a = 2 doubles the heights — peaks at 2, minimum at −2, giving range [−2; 2]; the period stays 360° because k = 1. Check by playing the first note: at x = 0, y = 2 cos(−60°) = 2 × 0,5 = 1 (cosine of a negative angle equals cosine of the positive one), so the sketch must cross the y-axis at 1 — which matches a curve rising towards its 60° peak.
